utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: After the break. Thank you very much. I guess this will then be a opportune time. Take the break and come back at a quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.text: Yes, this is -- this is a series of documents that we've had some discussion with the Prosecution about, and based on those discussions, and I don't want to assume that any assertions that are being made are necessarily accurate, we don't object to -- well, we object to the entirety of the documents, meaning all of them, being introduced on the grounds of relevance. Having said that, there are two things that we discussed with the Prosecution that we did not object to. One is the existence of indictments against General Mladic on two separate occasions; and, secondly, was the publication of those indictments. But all of the documents that are here, the entirety of these documents are not relevant, and we believe that the matter could be settled either by way of agreement or by way of introducing but a number of these documents, rather than all of them. I'm happy, for the moment, if further discussions with -- would seem to be fruitful to have all these documents MFI'd for the moment, and we can talk about it again. But I don't know if that is the case or not, and I certainly don't want to maintain that the position is anything other than I believe it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Those -- the position of counsel is correct. We did have those discussions. The relevance of these documents it is to demonstrate, Your Honour, that there was an indictment against General Mladic, that those -- that the indictment and the existence of the indictment was forwarded to the authorities in Bosnia and to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. There was forwarded to Federal Republic of Yugoslavia a request to advertise the existence of those indictments in respect of countries Bosnia and in the FRY, and these are the documents that are the underlying basis of that set of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you insist on them being admitted and not marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can mark them for identification and we can discuss these later, but I don't think we've going to advance the discussion any further, later. I'm happy to mark them for identification for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hope springs eternal so why don't we do that for the moment and see if we can do something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, would you MFI those, please.

All these personnel files which were admitted and which will be tendered in the future, the B/C/S is the whole document, the entire document. Where Mr. Harmon translated -- had portions translated into English and so I assume he is tendering those portions. Now, if the Defence wishes to tender some other portions which are in B/C/S in the existing system they would have to provide an English translation. What I want to say is that all documents that are being admitted into evidence now and which will be admitted in future that the B/C/S is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down. The interpreters --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are portions of the personnel files that are translated in English, portions that are untranslated. They are the whole files in some cases because the whole files are -- contain information that may or may not be relevant to counsel, to the Court. We have made an effort to translate what we consider to be significant parts of those files. Counsel can rely on the admission of the B/C/S file and under a document, under an exhibit number and make selections of their own that they deem is appropriate. So we are seeking the admission of the portions that are identified in the schedule, and the B/C/S remains -- some parts remain untranslated, obviously in the course of the trial, if counsel wants to rely on parts of those, he has the opportunity to do so.
